---
title: Search Files
---

SearcherKit provides a out-of-the-box local file search pipeline for agents to answer questions about files in a local directory, with the config `file_search`.

```bash
question -> LLM -> search -> ripgrep matches
                -> visit  -> complete file content
                -> LLM -> final answer
```

To use it, you should
- Install the required dependencies
- Configure enviroment variables for LLM and file search root
- Run searchagent tui with the `file_search` config.

### Install SearcherKit

SearcherKit requires Python 3.12 or later. Install the package in a virtual
environment:

:::: {.panel-tabset}
#### pip

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e .
```

#### uv

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate  # macOS/Linux
# Windows PowerShell: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
uv pip install -e .
```
::::

SearcherKit uses [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) to search through local files. Install with the [Installation Guide](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep#installation). 

To ensure that riggrep is available, run:
```bash
rg --version
```

### Configure the environment

SearcherKit with the `file_search` config uses the following environment variables.

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model name sent to the endpoint |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | Endpoint credential; use `EMPTY` only when the server permits it |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible API base URL |
| `FILE_SEARCH_ROOT` | Directory that `search` and `visit` may access; defaults to `./docs` |

For a one-time setup, define the variables in the terminal session where you
will start SearcherKit. The values remain available until that terminal is
closed.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Bash

```bash
export LLM_MODEL="YOUR_MODEL"
export LLM_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
export LLM_BASE_URL="https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
export FILE_SEARCH_ROOT="./docs"
```

#### PowerShell

```powershell
$env:LLM_MODEL = "YOUR_MODEL"
$env:LLM_API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY"
$env:LLM_BASE_URL = "https://your-endpoint.example/v1"
$env:FILE_SEARCH_ROOT = ".\docs"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
To keep the configuration across terminal sessions, create a `.env` file in
the directory where you run SearcherKit:

```dotenv
LLM_MODEL=YOUR_MODEL
LLM_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY
LLM_BASE_URL=https://your-endpoint.example/v1
FILE_SEARCH_ROOT=./docs
```

SearcherKit loads `.env` by default. Use `--env-file path/to/another.env` to load a
different file. Variables already defined in the terminal take precedence over
values in the dotenv file. 
:::

### Start to search files

```bash
searcher tui --config-path file_search
```

The source searches exact text fragments with smart case. Search results use
paths relative to `FILE_SEARCH_ROOT`; the visit tool reads those relative paths.
Paths outside the configured root are rejected.

Use `/tool-detail` to inspect tool arguments and results. Interactive records,
the global log, and trace logs are written under
`outputs/file-search-tui/interactive`.

For general controls and record behavior, see
[Use the Interactive TUI](../04-interface/02-use-the-interactive-tui.qmd). For the complete
source/tool model, see [Sources and Tools](../03-customizing/03-sources-and-tools.qmd).
